recentItems.title: Tom and Jerry | Full Episode Mega Compilation | Vol. 48 | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Tune in for hilarious full episodes of Tom and Jerry with Nibbles, Droopy, kittens, and more! 

Episodes in order:
The Little Orphan (1949): An orphan mouse joins Tom and Jerry for Thanksgiving Dinner. - disclaimer up until 4:50 :  

Love Me, Love My Mouse (1966): Tom falls in love and offers Jerry as a gift for the female cat but things turn a little unexpected when she lends a sympathetic ear to his plight.

Baby Puss (1943): A little girl makes Tom her baby cat, and Jerry along with some alley cats taunts the unfortunate feline.

The Mouse Comes to Dinner (1945): When Tom invites his lady friend to dinner, Jerry is there to screw it up.

Salt Water Tabby (1947): Tom's efforts to impress a female cat at the beach are foiled by Jerry and a crab.

The Brothers Carry-Mouse-Off (1965): Jerry uses radar to avoid any traps Tom has set up for him using food. Eventually Tom tries to dress up like a female mouse to trap Jerry, but he is foiled when other cats chase him.

The Two Mouseketeers (1952): Given the responsibility, by the tyrannical king, of guarding the grand banquet table, Tom is confronted by the sudden appearance of Jerry and Tuffy, the mouseketeers.

Shutter Bugged Cat (1967): Tired of his old experiments failing to catch Jerry, Tom gets an idea to revise one of them.

recentItems.title: Looney Tunes | Bugs, Porky, Daffy, Sylvester, Elmer, Yosemite Sam Mega Compilation | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Enjoy your favorite characters like Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Yosemite Sam, Elmer Fudd, and more in these classic Looney Tunes moments!

Episodes in order:
Rabbit of Seville (1950): Elmer's hunting for Bugs lands them both on stage at the Hollywood Bowl. They fight it out until they end up getting married in the final act.

The Scarlet Pumpernickel (1950): Sick of doing comedy, Daffy finally gets a dramatic role. The movie is about a swashbuckler who must battle the bad guys while saving his lady fair.

Walky Talky Hawky (1946): Henery goes out to fulfill his destiny: hunting chickens. Foghorn Leghorn is fighting with a dog and uses the naive Henery against his enemy.

What's Opera, Doc? (1957): Elmer Fudd is hunting Bugs Bunny and chases him into an opera acting out their characters.

Rabbit Seasoning (1966): Elmer is hunting both Daffy and Bugs again. Bugs talks Elmer into going after Daffy, who ends up getting the worst of all the pranks.
Tweet Dreams (1959): Sylvester realizes he has a fixation with Tweety and seeks help from a psychiatrist.

The Ducksters (1950): Daffy is an obnoxious radio host who puts the guest, Porky, through an arduous series of quizzes. The more questions he gets wrong, the more penalties Daffy gives him.

Drip-Along Daffy (1951): A western parody of a dangerous wilderness town and the hero that tries to fix it. Drip-Along Daffy is our hero on horseback and Porky Pig is the sidekick on a mule.

Hen House Henery (1949): Henery Hawk sets out to catch Foghorn but he scolds Henery and tells him to start small. Henery tries to get ducks or a turtle but fails. In the meantime Foghorn paints the dog's tongue green and then the dog and Henery team up on Foghorn.

Bugs Bunny Anniversary Collection: https://www.warnerbros.com/tv/bugs-bunny-anniversary-collection.

About Helen of Troy (Theatrical Release - January 26, 1956):
In an epic tale of passion, heroism, love, betrayal and war that has that has been passed from generation to generation since the dawn of civilization, one woman possesses a beauty that launches a thousand ships and sparks a war that destroys the greatest city of its age--Helen of Troy. 1100 BCE. King Priam (Sir Cedric Hardwicke) of Troy, sends his son, Paris (Jacques Sernas), to Sparta to negotiate a treaty to ensure peace between the two Greek city-states. But Paris falls in love with Spartan King Menelaus' (Niall MacGinnis) wife, Helen (Rossana Podesta). Paris kidnaps the willing Helen Podest and her servant (Brigitte Bardot), starting a war that will ultimately kill thousands of brave warriors and spell the end of the city of Troy.

Starring: Rossana Podestà as Helen, Jacques Sernas as Paris, Stanley Baker as Achilles, Niall MacGinnis as Menelaus, Robert Douglas as Agamemnon
Directed by: Robert Wise

recentItems.title: Tom and Jerry | Full Episode Mega Compilation | Vol. 47 | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Enjoy iconic full episodes of Tom and Jerry with Spike the bulldog, Droopy, kittens, and more! 

Episodes in order:
His Mouse Friday (1951): Lost at sea on a life raft, Tom washes ashore on a desserted island where he meets up with Jerry, posing as a cannibal.

The Yankee Doodle Mouse (1943): Tom is attacking Jerry with everything that's in the house. He throws vases, paper airplanes, lamps, and anything he can get his hands on to get Jerry. Basically, it's like a war is going on. Jerry retaliates by using a cheese grater, and using fireworks to fight Tom back with. (I.E. Yankee Doodle Mouse).

The Bodyguard (1944): Jerry uses a whistle given to him by a grateful bulldog to stop Tom from chasing him.

The Million Dollar Cat (1944): Tom will inherit a million dollars if he doesn't harm any living thing, including Jerry.

Triplet Trouble (1952): Tom's home is invaded with three new kittens that turn out to be more trouble than they are worth.

Mucho Mouse (1957): Tom, the "Olympic, U.S. and World Champion Mouse Catcher," heads to Spain to catch "El Magnifico" (Jerry).

Cat Napping (1951): Tom's getting ready to settle into the hammock, but Jerry has beat him to it and the battle begins.

recentItems.title: Looney Tunes | Yosemite Sam, Bugs Bunny Mega Compilation | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Yosemite Sam is after Bugs Bunny again as a knight, hunter, pirate, and more in these classic hilarious Looney Tunes episode moments!

Episodes in order:
Knighty Knight Bugs (1958): Bugs is a hapless court jester who sneaks into the villain's castle while Black Knight Sam is snoozing. Bugs makes off with the sword with Sam chasing him the whole way and holes up in Sam's castle not letting him in. As Bugs tries to sneak out Sam and his fire breathing lizard sneak in and all three of them find themselves in the explosives room. When the lizard sneezes he converts the entire turret of the castle into a rocket heading straight for the moon.

Mutiny on the Bunny (1950): Shanghai Sam tricks Bugs into sailing with him and then makes him do all the work. Bugs takes control of the boat angering Sam who shoots at the boat. When the boat sinks Sam and Bugs have to use the lifeboat to get back to shore.

Piker's Peak (1957): Bugs and Sam are in a race to see who can climb to the top of Schmatterhorn first and win 50,000 cronkites. Sam tries every trick he knows to make Bugs lose the race, but all these tricks backfire on him and he loses the race.

Rabbitson Crusoe (1956): Sam, playing Crusoe, lives on one of three little islands where he is trapped because of a shark named Dopey Dick. When Bugs appears on the island, Sam tries to eat him because he is tired of eating coconuts everyday, but through a series of pranks Bugs manages to get away.

Captain Hareblower (1954): Captain Bugs of his ship battles Pirate Yosemite Sam.

Bunker Hill Bunny (1950): The historic Revolutionary War battle at Bagel Heights is fought between Bugs and Yosemite.

Hare Trimmed (1953): Granny finds herself in a love triangle between Sam and Bugs both fighting for her hand in marriage, Sam for money, Bugs for good deeds. Sam tries to seduce her and Bugs challenges Sam to a gentlemen's dual. Bugs cleverly disguises himself as Granny and tricks Sam into doing a lot of painful things.

About The Candidate (Theatrical Release - June 30, 1972):
More powerful today than at the time of its 1972 release, The Candidate is a timeless tale of contemporary politics; expertly written by Oscar winner Jeremy Larner.

Robert Redford plays Bill McKay, an idealistic California attorney running for office in this marvelous, biting, satire on media-age political campaigns.

The stellar cast includes Peter Boyle and Melvyn Douglas, who also give memorable performances.

Starring: Robert Redford, Peter Boyle, Melvyn Douglas
Directed by: Michael Ritchie

About Casablanca (Theatrical Release - November 26, 1942):
Academy Award winners Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman light up the screen in one of the most enduring romances in movie history--Casablanca. Rick Blaine (Bogart--The African Queen, The Caine Mutiny) owns a nightclub in Vichy-controlled Casablanca, frequented by refugees desperate to escape German domination. Despite the ever-present human misery, Rick manages to remain uninvolved in World War II now raging across Europe and Northern Africa. But all that changes when Ilsa Lund (Bergman--Gaslight, Notorious) walks through the front door of Rick's club--Rick must now choose between a life with the woman he loves and becoming the hero that both she and the world need.​

Starring:  Humphrey Bogart as Rick, Ingrid Bergman as Ilsa
Directed by: Michael Curtiz

Welcome to Warner Classics - your gateway to the enchanting world of timeless movies and iconic performances from the Golden Age of Hollywood! Dive into a treasure trove of cinematic splendor, where every clip tells a story and every scene captivates the soul.

Join us on a journey through the annals of film history as we showcase unforgettable moments from the silver screen. Including Hollywood's brightest stars, our channel is a celebration of artistry and nostalgia that will transport you to a bygone era of glamour and sophistication.

recentItems.title: Tom and Jerry | Halloween Mega Compilation | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Jump into Spooky Season with full episodes of Tom and Jerry Halloween themed featuring Witches, Ghosts, and magical potions! 

Episodes in order:
The Invisible Mouse (1947): Jerry turns invisible after diving into a bottle of invisible ink and then gets back at Tom.

Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Mouse (1947): Jerry drinks a potion that makes him grow to the size of a giant. He decides to go after Tom, because THIS time he's bigger. Once the potion wears off, Tom drinks some of it, and he gets bigger. They do this over and over again. Academy Award nominee for 1948 Best Short Subject.

Fraidy Cat (1942): After Tom gets scared from listening to The Witching Hour on the radio Jerry schemes a way to keep him scared.

The Flying Sorceress (1956): Tom steals a witch's flying broom so he can scare the wits out of Jerry.
 
The Missing Mouse (1953): Jerry takes advantage of Tom's fear of an exploding white mouse by dunking himself in white shoe polish.

Purr-Chance to Dream (1967): Tom isn't sleeping well and keeps having nightmares about getting beat up by a bulldog.

Is There A Doctor In The Mouse (1964): Drinking a potion he mixed together helps Jerry beat Tom to all the food.
